annotations.title: Three-Factor Decomposition: πN/8 × 6/π² × 2/3 = N/(2π)
annotations.content: The density N/(2π) decomposes cleanly into three independent factors: (1) sector area gives πN/8 lattice points, (2) coprime density gives fraction 6/π², (3) parity correction gives fraction 2/3. Each factor comes from a different area of mathematics.

annotations.title: The Parity Involution (m,n) ↔ (m, m-n)
annotations.content: The map (m,n) → (m, m-n) is a bijection on coprime pairs in the triangle {0 < n < m} that swaps EO↔OO parity classes (since if m is odd and n is odd, m-n is even, and vice versa). This proves |EO| = |OO| within each triangle, reducing the 2/3 parity fraction to showing |OO| = 1/3.

annotations.title: Coprime Sector Count Grows to Infinity
annotations.content: coprimeInSectorCount(N) → ∞ as N → ∞. This follows from the sector point count growing as πN/8 and the coprime fraction being asymptotically 6/π² > 0.

annotations.title: Computational Verification
annotations.content: The counting functions are verified via native_decide for small values: primitiveTripleCount(0)=0, primitiveTripleCount(5)=1 (the 3-4-5 triple), primitiveTripleCount(13)=2, etc. This provides confidence in the definitions before proving asymptotic results.

annotations.title: Per-Column Involution Analysis
annotations.content: The global parity result is decomposed column-by-column: for each fixed m, the involution n ↔ m-n acts within the column. Per-column OE=OO equality is proved for small columns and extended via monotonicity arguments.
